incidents.title: APT36 mass-produces 'vibeware' implants with AI tools
incidents.targets: Indian government networks and related entities
models: unspecified LLMs and AI coding tools
incidents.outcome: High volume of disposable, often low-quality implants in Nim, Zig, Crystal, Rust and Go using Slack, Discord, Google Sheets and Supabase for C2.
incidents.confidenceReason: Bitdefender links the campaign to APT36 with medium confidence and attributes AI-assisted generation; direct fetch of the page was blocked (403) so claims rest on search-result summaries.
incidents.summary: Bitdefender describes an AI-assisted malware assembly line producing many variants in niche languages to overwhelm signature detection. Code quality was often poor, with missing C2 addresses.
incidents.quote: For exmaple, APT36, aka Transparent Tribe, is using vibe-coding — the practice of using conversational, natural language prompts to develop code with AI tools — to generate malware in obscure programming languages like Nim, Zig, and Crystal.

harness.note: AI-assisted malware generation, no agent harness named

incidents.title: Go dropper asks GPT-4 whether to deploy Sliver
incidents.outcome: The Sliver payload ran only when the model approved.
incidents.confidenceReason: Unit 42's code analysis shows the dropper sends host data 'to OpenAI's GPT-4 model using an HTTP API' and runs Sliver only on the model's verdict. Malware that calls a model as it runs is direct evidence of AI use, so the grade is Confirmed. Unit 42 reports 'No campaign or victims identified'.
incidents.summary: Unit 42 analyzed a Go dropper that sends host telemetry to GPT-4 and runs its Sliver payload only if the model says to execute, plus a .NET stealer whose GPT-3.5 calls were mostly theatre.
incidents.quote: Unit 42 analysed a Golang dropper that sends host telemetry to GPT-4 posing as an OPSEC AI and only runs its Sliver payload if the model returns execute true, plus a .NET stealer whose GPT-3.5 calls were mostly theatre.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep, which AI Threat Watch restates.
